latest_release.name: v8.5.0
latest_release.body:
Windows release binaries are signed through SignPath. See the Code signing policy: https://amiberry.com/code-signing-policy

## Highlights

### Licensing and third-party code
- WHDLoad, JST and the Kickstart RTB files are no longer bundled. "Update WHDBooter files" and `--download-whdboot` now get them from their authors' sites:
  - WHDLoad comes from whdload.de on every update, so new WHDLoad releases arrive.
  - The SKick RTB files are fetched once, only while one is missing, from Aminet `util/boot/skick346.lha`. That archive is checked against a fixed SHA-256 before it is unpacked.
  - JST comes from Aminet `game/patch/jst.lha`, only when "Use JST instead of WHDLoad" is on.
  - `kick31034.A1000.RTB` is still bundled.
  - A downloaded file replaces the installed one only after it matches the size and CRC in its LhA header. Only one download runs at a time, and none starts while a machine is running unpaused.
  
  (#2540)
- If WHDLoad is missing when a WHDLoad game boots, Amiberry shows a message that says where to get it. Nothing is downloaded automatically. The Paths panel and the `--download-whdboot` help name the sources (#2540)
- In older releases, "Update WHDBooter files" now gets "not found" for the removed files. The installed copies are kept, and the update reports a partial failure (#2540, #2549)
- WHDBooter's quit-on-exit now uses `host-quit` from Host-Tools 2.8 (GPL-3) instead of AmiQuit, a third-party binary with no source or licence. host-quit also works on Kickstart 1.3 and the 68000 (#2549, #2550)
- LhA archives are now read with Lhasa 0.6.0 (ISC) instead of LHa for UNIX, whose licence is not free. The rare `-lh2-` and `-lh3-` compression methods are no longer decoded (#2558)
- Each LhA member's CRC is now checked, so a corrupt member fails instead of returning bad data. Truncated or corrupt archives fail cleanly; a corrupt `-lh5-`/`-lh6-`/`-lh7-` archive used to crash the old decoder. LhA's `0xff` path separators are read as `/` (#2540, #2558)
- PearPC was removed. It was never compiled into any build, so choosing it left the machine with no PPC at all. PPC emulation uses the QEMU plugin only. A configuration with `ppc_implementation=pearpc` loads as `auto` without a warning and is saved as `auto` (#2554)
- Licence clean-up:
  - The UAE portability headers and `vm.cpp` were rewritten under GPL-3.0-or-later, with no change in behaviour (#2552).
  - Third-party licence notices were corrected: HRTMon 2.37 is GPL-2.0-or-later, the Warp decruncher is LGPL-2.1-or-later, mos6502 is MIT (its source files now carry the notice) and iff.library is public domain. `gamecontrollerdb.txt` carries its zlib notice, unlzx credits all its authors, and Amiberry's copy of mt32emu is distributed under GPL-3.0-or-later, as section 3 of the LGPL 2.1 allows (#2557).
- Each release now includes `amiberry-<tag>-third-party-sources.tar.xz`. It holds the exact source of the GPL and LGPL libraries bundled in the macOS release (such as FFmpeg, x264, x265, LAME, mpg123, libmpeg2 and libserialport), checked against Homebrew's checksums, and is listed in `SHA256SUMS` (#2556)
- The Amiga libraries some WHDLoad games need are no longer inside `boot-data.zip`, because their licences don't allow bundling them. "Update WHDBooter files" downloads them from their Aminet packages while one is missing; every file is checked against its CRC, and the packages that never change are also checked against a fixed SHA-256 (MMULib, which its author updates in place, isn't). They go into the WHDBoot folder's `Libs` drawer, which the booter mounts as `DH4:` and adds to `LIBS:`, so `LIBS:Compressors` works too. Existing files are never overwritten (#2559):
  - the XPK libraries: `xpkmaster.library` and 16 compressors, from `util/pack/xpk_User`;
  - MMULib's `68040.library`, now with the `mmu.library` and `680x0.library` it needs, which the old zip lacked, from `util/libs/MMULib`;
  - `explode.library`, from `util/libs/explode-7`;
  - OctaMED's `medplayer.library
